icons.name: turn-taking
icons.heading: Turn taking
icons.description: The caller yields the floor and the agent takes it. Light: the floor token hops up inside the caller's bubble, swells and drops out through its bottom, falls on a curve into the agent's bubble, landing with a hit; the agent's bubble pops as it takes the floor and settles. Strong: the token gathers higher, the caller's bubble recoils as it lets go, the token lands with a bounce, and the agent's bubble pops harder. Reverse: the token is tossed back up into the caller's bubble, which pops as it takes the floor again.

Light: the detector sweeps ten units along the sampling rail; as it reaches the end, the language glyph is identified and pops (it swells with its crossbar, snaps back and settles), and the detector glides home. Strong: the detector draws back before a faster sweep, and the glyph pops harder with a second, smaller swing. The speech card never moves.

Strong: the hand ticks back before a faster lap, and the clock rings harder with more swings. The quiet utterance and the waiting dash never move.

icons.name: dtmf-input
icons.heading: DTMF input
icons.description: A keypad key is pressed and sounds its dual tone. Light: the key is pushed in (it shrinks into the panel with a hit) and springs back; a beat later both tone waves ring at once, their amplitude swelling and decaying, the low tone in one slow swing and the high tone in quicker flutters. Strong: the key lifts a touch before a harder press, and both tones ring louder and longer. The waves never leave their lines.

icons.name: on-hold
icons.heading: On hold
icons.description: The call is parked on hold. Light: the receiver is set down 1.5 units onto its rest with a hit and a small bounce, then the pause sign rises out of the two dots, the left bar first and the right one just after, each overshooting a touch and settling. Strong: the receiver is lifted first and set down harder with a double bounce, and the bars shoot up further before settling. Reverse: the pause bars collapse back into dots, right then left, and the receiver is picked up again.

icons.name: escalation-flag
icons.heading: Escalation flag
icons.description: A call issue is escalated: the problem call shakes, then the flag is hoisted to the top of the pole and catches the wind. Light: the call bubble gives a quick alarm shake, the flag runs ten units up the fixed pole, stops dead at the top and flutters, settling flat. Strong: the bubble shakes harder, the flag gathers low, is hoisted past the top and settles back onto it, and flutters longer. Reverse: the flag is lowered down the pole and lands at its old place; the call does not shake again.

icons.name: voicemail-detection
icons.heading: Voicemail detection
icons.description: An answering-machine greeting plays and the detector recognises it. Light: the three greeting syllables swell in turn, left to right; the pupil glances to the first and follows them across, then snaps back to centre and dilates: machine detected. Strong: the greeting plays two phrases, the pupil searches wider, and the recognition beat is bigger with a second, smaller swing. The greeting card and the eye outline never move.

Light: the three greeting syllables swell in turn, left to right; the pupil glances to the first and follows them across, then snaps back to centre and dilates: machine detected. Strong: the greeting plays two phrases, the pupil searches wider, and the recognition beat is bigger with a second, smaller swing. The greeting card and the eye outline never move.
